title: IRIS: A 8.55mJ/frame Spatial Computing SoC for Interactable Rendering and Surface-Aware Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: Interactive Spatial Computing (ISC) for mixed-reality (MR) requires real-time surface-aware modeling (SAM) and interactive photorealistic rendering (IPR) with tight latency budgets (15ms) and high computational demands. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables superior quality but faces three challenges: (1) massive external memory access (EMA) for unordered >50MB parameters exceeds edge GPU L2 cache (4MB), (2) IPR requires three sequential stages (deform/reflect/render) causing 2.33x overhead vs. non-interactive rendering, (3) backpropagation for SAM consumes 55.8% of compute due to FP16 precision and limited reusability.
motivation: Mixed-reality applications demand immersive, deformable 3D object manipulation in real-time on mobile/edge devices; NeRF accelerators cannot support surface extraction and deformation required for ISC, necessitating specialized 3DGS hardware.
method: IRIS compresses the 3D Gaussian parameters using Single-Embedding-Multi-MLP (a single compact data representation fed to multiple small neural networks), reducing the over 50MB of data while maintaining visual quality. It features custom processor circuits specifically designed for surface-aware 3D modeling and interactive photorealistic rendering, keeping data in the fast on-chip cache (4MB) instead of requiring slow external memory access, and reuses hardware components during backpropagation (the computationally expensive training step that consumed 55.8% of the work in older approaches). Scheduling and memory orchestration keep all processing within the 15-millisecond latency budget required for real-time interaction.
key_novelty: IRIS is the first processor chip built specifically for real-time mixed-reality rendering using 3D Gaussian Splatting, achieving 8.55 millijoules per frame through neural-network data compression and hardware that jointly optimizes surface modeling, rendering, and training.
contributions: SEMM-based 3DGS compression reducing EMA from 81.3% to 52.8% of system energy
15ms latency IPR for real-time user interaction on mobile edge devices
Integrated SAM+IPR+backprop hardware reducing backprop compute to <45% of total via reuse
8.55mJ/frame energy efficiency enabling multi-frame/second performance on battery-powered MR headsets

metrics.other: SAM: <20min (vs >20min on edge GPU), IPR: <400ms (vs >400ms baseline)

primary_theme: Edge SoC for real-time interactive 3D Gaussian Splatting in MR
